evidence: Inspected the current page and actual alg-gradient-descent body. It specifies finite gradient updates and has no general convergence conclusion. The local 4DVAR algorithm calls it for at most a stated finite iteration limit and makes no convergence claim. This is a current-body interface check only; no additional acceptance is asserted.

Inspected the current draft A page, batch-43 manifest and actual bodies for def-fixed-interval-gaussian-smoothing-law, lem-backward-gaussian-kernel-is-valid-under-full-smoothing-data, alg-rauch-tung-striebel-smoother, and thm-rauch-tung-striebel-fixed-interval-recursion. The definition supplies a data-indexed RCD smoothing target without asserting existence; the theorem proves the Gaussian RTS version by backward kernel integration and requires each forecast covariance it inverts to be positive definite. The assigned definition uses that smoothing convention, and the A-page note states the RTS inverse-domain condition. Batch-43 records the four suppliers ready, but this inspection is not independent mathematical approval.

Inspected the actual BCS-38 definition and existence theorem. The definition gives data-indexed filtering and predictive conditional-law kernels and a full-path smoothing kernel on standard-Borel histories, with null-history version freedom; the existence theorem states and proves finite-horizon kernel-law existence. The local finite-dimensional maps are Borel measurable and the definition imports only those stated conventions. BCS-38 is a draft supplier; no acceptance is inferred.

This page is a transitive BCS-40 prerequisite and the direct source page for def-data-assimilation-problem's filtering, predictive, and full-path smoothing vocabulary. The current page and BCS-38 definition/existence proof bodies were inspected; their standard-Borel and AC hypotheses match the local data-indexed RCD wording. Draft interface verification only.

Inspected the current BCS-39 page, alg-kalman-filter and thm-kalman-filter-is-exact-posterior bodies, plus batch-42 notes and the owner's final citation-resolution record. The algorithm permits PSD/singular state and noise covariances and solves only SPD innovation matrices; the exact-filter theorem uses the same admissibility condition. Its BCS-03 conditional-normal supplier's inline product-law and Tonelli labels were corrected, and its current body has the corrected labels. The relevant Step-1 records report authoring-ready status; no independent approval is asserted.

The actual BCS-39 statement gives the exact filtering-kernel version under AC, PSD covariance blocks, and SPD innovation matrices. The 3DVAR theorem uses an admissible one-step identity-transition, zero-process-covariance model with innovation S=HBH^T+Gamma, which is SPD because Gamma is SPD. The exact-filter supplier body and current batch-42 resolution were inspected; the result remains a draft interface, not independent approval.

The local reference-ensemble statement requires each R_k to be SPD, so its deterministic Kalman innovation S_k=H_kP_{k|k-1}H_k^T+R_k is SPD even when P_0 and Q_k are singular. The inspected BCS-39 exact-filter theorem permits those PSD singular covariances and provides the matching conditional-law version. Draft-body compatibility only.

The EnKF limit theorem fixes T and assumes R_k positive definite at each time; the reference covariance therefore has SPD innovation matrices. The inspected BCS-39 statement proves the exact filtering law at each fixed data history under AC while allowing singular PSD state/process covariance. This is a current interface check, not independent approval.

The published Cholesky theorem's SPD hypothesis matches S=HBH^T+Gamma in the local algorithm: for nonzero z, z^TSz=(H^Tz)^TB(H^Tz)+z^TGamma z>0. The algorithm uses the positive-diagonal factor and two triangular solves, not an unverified inverse.
